Definitions

Workplace glossary

Plain definitions of the terms that come up around productivity, pay and monitoring. Each entry gives the definition first, then what the rule or the research actually says, and what the term is commonly confused with.

All terms

11 definitions
Time Tracking

Comp Time

Compensatory time, or comp time, is paid time off granted in place of overtime pay. Under the Fair Labor Standards Act it is available only to public agencies, and it must accrue at one and a half hours for every overtime hour worked.

Productivity

Deep Work

Deep work is professional activity performed in a state of distraction-free concentration that pushes cognitive capability to its limit. Its opposite is shallow work: logistical tasks performed while distracted, which are easy to replicate.

Engagement

eNPS

eNPS, or employee Net Promoter Score, is the percentage of employees who would recommend the organisation as a place to work minus the percentage who would not, on a 0 to 10 scale.

Time Tracking

Exempt vs Non-Exempt Employee

An exempt employee is one the Fair Labor Standards Act excludes from its minimum wage and overtime requirements, because they are paid on a salary basis at or above a set threshold and their actual job duties fall within a recognised exemption.

Burnout

Presenteeism

Presenteeism is working while unwell or otherwise impaired, so the person is present but not functioning at full capacity. Its cost is usually larger than absenteeism because it is invisible in attendance data.

Engagement

Quiet Cracking

Quiet cracking is a persistent sense of unhappiness at work that erodes motivation and performance while the employee stays in the role, typically because leaving feels too risky.

Engagement

Quiet Firing

Quiet firing is making someone's job worse until they resign, rather than managing or dismissing them. It is usually avoidance rather than strategy, and it transfers the cost of a decision onto the employee.

Time Tracking

Shift Differential

Shift differential is extra pay for working a less desirable shift, such as nights, weekends or holidays. It is a voluntary practice under federal law, but it must be included in the regular rate when overtime is calculated.

Productivity

Span of Control

Span of control is the number of direct reports a single manager has. A wide span means many reports and a flatter organisation; a narrow span means fewer reports and more layers.

Engagement

Turnover Rate

Turnover rate is the number of employees who left during a period, divided by the average headcount over that period, expressed as a percentage.

Productivity

Workforce Analytics

Workforce analytics is the analysis of aggregated workforce data to understand how work gets done and to inform staffing, capacity and process decisions.
